Didactic plots of backtests and tuning

Source: R/compare.R
mt_plot_design.Rd

  • mt_plot_backtest_design() shows the training and test years of each origin of a rolling-origin backtest: every model is fitted to the years up to the origin and scored on the years after it.

  • mt_plot_pit() shows the histogram of the probability integral transform (PIT: the share of forecast draws below the observed value) per model. Calibrated forecasts give a flat histogram; a U shape means intervals that are too narrow, a hump in the middle intervals that are too wide, a slope a bias.

  • mt_plot_tuning() shows the scores of the settings of mt_tune() with one standard error, the chosen setting highlighted.

Usage

mt_plot_backtest_design(data, origins, h)

mt_plot_tuning(tune)

mt_plot_pit(
  backtest,
  target = c("rate", "life_expectancy", "asr", "life_expectancy_gap", "asr_gap"),
  bins = 10
)

Arguments

data

An mt_data object (its years).

origins

Forecast origins (last training years).

h

Horizon.

tune

The result of mt_tune().

backtest

An mt_backtest() result.

target

"rate", "life_expectancy", "asr", "life_expectancy_gap" or "asr_gap" (see quantities and contrast in mt_backtest()).

bins

Number of histogram bins.

Value

A ggplot object.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 1990:2012)
  mt_plot_backtest_design(x, origins = 2003:2007, h = 5)
}
